scope: Eight bounded CPU FDE preprocessing/reference-distance contracts; partial JMP19.2 method coverage, not full platform or undocumented-default equivalence.
integration_status: Public execute/formal tests,production exported C ABI fixtures and matching native SQL PASS;bounded partial contracts only
primary_research_notes: JMP19.2 Data Processing and Baseline Correction Reports read directly. The latter explicitly says validation functions are not baseline-corrected.

Ryan1988 original article publisher access403; the original seven-page article reprint was read, including log-log compression (without square root), broad-width clipping and separate low-statistics/FWHM filter. Only the explicit span-clipping variant is implemented.

Baek2015 original author-repository PDF was available as indexed full text, including equations9/10 and algorithm pseudocode; live repository access returned502/DNS failure. Algorithm matches that method contract, not an unverified JMP implementation.

common_contract.data: Nonempty finite long rows[x,y,id] or[x,y,id,role], uniform width3/4,<=100000 observations,<=128functions,<=10000observations/function. IDs exact integers within absolute2^53-1. Role0=analysis/training(default),1=validation; a single ID cannot mix roles.
common_contract.args: <=16384 finite doubles with exact operation-specific count/ranges.
common_contract.ordering: Function IDs preserve first appearance; observations sorted by x, then original row index for ties. Grid/baseline methods require distinct x; binning/thinning/DTW retain repeated observations explicitly.
common_contract.baseline_validation: SNIP/arWLS/supplied-baseline transform role0 curves only. Role1 original values pass unchanged, baseline/weights zero placeholders, applied=false and arWLS convergence=null. This does not mean a zero baseline was estimated.
common_contract.uncertainty: No inferential p-values, SEs or confidence bands are claimed for preprocessing or curve-distance rankings. Convergence concerns the specified numerical iteration only.
common_contract.resource_limits: SNIP sum(training lengths)*max_halfwindow<=200000000; arWLS sum(training lengths)*maxiter*16<=200000000; DTW pair n*m<=4000000 and total unordered or target/candidate cell pairs<=200000000.
common_contract.uniform_grid_tolerance: 1e-8*spacing+8*machine_epsilon*max(abs(x)); no implicit resampling before baseline methods.
common_contract.numeric: Reject unresolved/rank-singular penalty systems and nonrepresentable required arithmetic. Null output is reserved for declared empty bins, outside-support values, skipped diagnostics or nonconvergence diagnostics. No JSON NaN/Infinity tokens.
common_contract.inference_boundary: No GUI selection semantics, FPC model fitting, golden-curve optimization, Fourier/basis/FDA model expansion is added here.

operations.data: Long function observations,>=2 distinct x per ID; internally sorted. Auto/size-only grid estimates use only role0 functions. Explicit bounds/size requires no training rows.
args: []:size=min(4096,longest training function),domain=intersection of training supports,outside null
[size]:integer2..min(4096,longest training function); training-domain intersection
[size,lower,upper,outside_policy]:size2..4096,lower<upper; all quantities supplied, so validation-only replay and size larger than query sample count are supported
outside_policy:0=null beyond support,1=constant endpoint extension,2=reject; required in full layout
operations.estimator: Piecewise linear interpolation on a single evenly spaced grid. The full-argument layout replays a stored grid and estimates no new statistics. Auto bounds/length never use validation curves. Endpoints are exact, interior weights are convex; grids finer than representable x spacing reject. Null values explicitly mean unsupported query locations under policy0. Full explicit replay extends the JMP-style automatic longest-function size limit; it is an implementation contract, not an undocumented JMP default claim.

operations.description: SNIP peak clipping on uniform grids: [x,y,id,optional role]; [max_halfwindow,transform0raw/1Ryan-loglog=1,direction0increasing/1decreasing=0].
operations.data: Training IDs require an evenly spaced strictly increasing x grid and n>=2*max_halfwindow+1. Validation IDs pass unchanged without fitting; their baseline arrays are zero placeholders with baseline_applied=false. Log-log input Y>=0; raw transform allows signed Y.
args: max_halfwindow:required integer1..4999,also <=(n-1)/2 for every training ID
transform:0=identity,1=G(y)=ln(ln(1+y)+1);default1; original Ryan log-log transform has no square root
direction:0=widths1..max,1=max..1;default0; each pass reads the previous entire vector synchronously
operations.estimator: At each width w replace z_i by min(z_i,(z_(i-w)+z_(i+w))/2) where both neighbors exist; retain other points. Invert G after clipping and return baseline plus Y-baseline. This is an explicit span-scheduled SNIP variant based on peak clipping and Ryan double-log compression. It does not implement the full original energy-dependent FWHM/adaptive low-statistics filter, later LLS square-root variant, or unknown JMP settings. Clipping is distinct from a moving average.

operations.saved_reference_contract: Persist per-curve result.x/result.baselines as an explicit baseline function and reuse via functional_baseline with a separate reference ID. This is supplied-reference reuse, not refitting SNIP on validation curves.

operations.data: Training IDs require >=3 uniformly spaced distinct x values. Validation rows remain unchanged with zero placeholder baseline/weights, convergence null, baseline_applied=false.
args: lambda:1e-8..1e10,default1e5; penalty on index-based second differences
weight_tolerance:1e-12..1e-2,default1e-6; L2 relative proposed-versus-used weight change
maxiter:integer1..1000,default100
negative_std_ddof:0=population,1=sample;default0; explicit convention because exact software defaults are not assumed
operations.estimator: Solve (W+lambda D2^T D2)z=Wy with a true pentadiagonal Cholesky factorization. Start weights1; for d=y-z, estimate m,s from negative residuals and propose w_i=1/(1+exp(2*(d_i-(-m+2s))/s)), as Baek2015 arPLS (called ARWLS in JMP menu). Stop on relative weight change and small linear backward error. Returned weights are the weights that actually solved the returned baseline, not an unsolved next proposal. Zero/unidentified negative noise scale, iteration limits or numerical linear failures never claim convergence. No hidden ridge or weight floor. Affine signals within numeric tolerance have zero second-difference baseline correction and converge without iterations.

operations.saved_reference_contract: No global learned carrier: baseline is fitted independently for each role0 function. Persist x/baselines and load as a supplied baseline reference if desired. Validation functions are not silently baseline-corrected or refitted.

operations.description: Subtract an explicit baseline function: [x,y,id,optional role]; [baseline_id,outside0null/1constant/2reject=2].
operations.data: Baseline ID must exist with role0,>=2 distinct x; its observations are a supplied reference and excluded from corrected IDs. Other training IDs may be irregular. Validation IDs pass unchanged.
args: baseline_id:required exact ID of supplied reference function
outside_policy:0=null,1=constant endpoint extension,2=reject;default2
operations.estimator: Linearly interpolate the supplied baseline to each training function x and subtract it. Return original data, interpolated baselines, corrected data and applied flags. Null outside support follows explicit policy0. The reference is neither estimated from other curves nor included in corrected candidates. A role1 validation function cannot be repurposed as a training baseline.

operations.saved_reference_contract: Persist a supplied or computed reference as [x,baseline,reference_id,0] rows. Append those same rows to any new role0 analysis curves and call the same reference ID. Role1 curves deliberately remain unchanged, matching the documented validation policy.

operations.data: >=2 functions in within-ID sorted x order; unequal lengths permitted. Each ID has at least1 point. X determines sequence order, not a physical-time cost.
args: window:-1=unconstrained,otherwise integer0..longest length; must reach every pair endpoint
normalize:0=original intensities,1=per-curve mean/population-standard-deviation standardization;default0; constant curves reject under1
cost:0=squared local amplitude difference and square root of summed path cost,1=absolute local difference and summed cost;default0
operations.estimator: Sakoe-Chiba-band DTW with diagonal/up/left predecessor steps, two-row dynamic programming. Compute each unordered pair once and mirror it, diagonal0. Normalization is independently within each supplied curve, with scale-safe arithmetic; no training-set fitting. Window infeasibility or resource excess rejects rather than widening the window. DTW distances need not satisfy the triangle inequality. This contract supplies the numerical matrix for downstream clustering; it does not construct a JMP report script.

operations.description: Supplied golden/reference curve distance ranking: [x,y,id,optional role]; [target_id,metric0RMSE/1MAE/2DTW=0,window=-1,normalize=0].
operations.data: >=2 functions; explicit target ID excluded from candidate scores/ranking. RMSE/MAE require identical ordered x grids; DTW allows unequal lengths. Curve roles retained for candidate provenance.
args: target_id:required exact ID of pre-specified reference/golden curve
metric:0=RMSE,1=MAE,2=squared-cost square-root DTW;default0
window:-1=unconstrained,otherwise valid DTW radius;default-1
normalize:0=original intensities,1=independent per-curve population standardization;default0
operations.estimator: Compare each candidate with a supplied target, return scores in input function order and ascending ranking, deterministic ties by candidate order. Target is never included among candidates or used to estimate a common curve/model. Stable RMS avoids overflowing an intermediate unnormalized Euclidean norm. This is explicit distance matching, not FPC-score desirability profiling, model fitting, or process-setting optimization.
